docs.title: pyscio Documentation
docs.text: pyscio is an autonomous statistical inference engine, one-tap exploratory data analysis (EDA) suite, multivariate regression toolkit, and pure numerical hypothesis testing framework for Python (>= 3.11).

docs.title: Architectural Layers
docs.text:
pyscio enforces a strict 5-layer downward dependency graph:

  1. pyscio.core (L0): Immutable result containers (TestResult, RegressionResult, EDAReport, ScreenReport, SVGFigure), typed domain exceptions (StatError, SampleSizeError, ZeroVarError), 8-role semantic column classification (Role), universal DataFrame coercion (ensure_pandas_df), and HTML/Rich/LaTeX/Markdown/APA/SVG renderers.
  2. pyscio.functional as F (L1): Stateless, deterministic NumPy/SciPy mathematical kernels returning lightweight NamedTuples (TTestResult, ANOVAResult, RMAnovaResult, NonParametricResult, TOSTResult, CorrelationResult, BayesFactorResult).
  3. pyscio.models (L2): Wilkinson formula design matrix parser (parse_formula), Ordinary Least Squares (ols with QR decomposition and MacKinnon-White HC0–HC3 robust standard errors), Type II & Type III Factorial ANOVA (anova_table), Newton-Raphson IRLS binary logistic regression (logistic), Poisson log-linear GLM (poisson with QMLE HC3 SEs & IRR), and Linear Mixed-Effects Models (mixedlm via Profiled REML/ML).
  4. pyscio.stat & pyscio.eda (L3): Autonomous assumption-checked decision router (compare, screen, tost, solve_power) and vectorized exploratory data analysis (read, profile, audit_quality, correlations, vif).
  5. pyscio.integrations & pyscio.cli (L4): Native Pandas (df.scio) and Polars (pl_df.scio) DataFrame accessors, dual-backend statistical plotting (plot_raincloud, .plot()), and the pyscio command-line interface.

docs.title: Top-Level Namespace (pyscio)
docs.text:
• sc.read(source, **kwargs) — Multi-format tabular reader (CSV/TSV, Parquet, Excel, JSON).
  • sc.compare(data, x, y, *, alpha=0.05, paired=False, alternative="two-sided", mu=0.0, formula=None) — Autonomous hypothesis testing router.
  • sc.screen(df, y, *, alpha=0.05, features=None) — Multi-feature discovery screening with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control.
  • sc.ols(df, formula, *, robust_se="HC3", alpha=0.05) — Ordinary Least Squares regression with HC0–HC3 robust standard errors.
  • sc.logistic(df, formula, *, alpha=0.05, max_iter=50, tol=1e-6) — Binary logistic regression via Newton-Raphson IRLS.
  • sc.tost(a, b=None, *, low=-0.5, high=0.5, bound=None, alpha=0.05, paired=False, popmean=0.0) — Two One-Sided Tests for statistical equivalence.

docs.title: Parametric & Non-Parametric Tests
docs.text:
• F.student_t(a, b, alternative="two-sided", conf_level=0.95) -> TTestResult
  • F.welch_t(a, b, alternative="two-sided", conf_level=0.95) -> TTestResult
  • F.paired_t(a, b, alternative="two-sided", conf_level=0.95) -> TTestResult
  • F.one_sample_t(a, popmean=0.0, alternative="two-sided", conf_level=0.95) -> TTestResult
  • F.anova(*groups) -> ANOVAResult
  • F.welch_anova(*groups) -> ANOVAResult
  • F.mann_whitney(a, b, alternative="two-sided") -> NonParametricResult
  • F.wilcoxon(a, b=None, alternative="two-sided") -> NonParametricResult
  • F.kruskal(*groups) -> NonParametricResult
  • F.chisq(observed, correct=True) -> ChiSqResult
  • F.fisher(table, alternative="two-sided") -> FisherResult

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
uv add pyscio
# or
pip install pyscio

docs.title: 1. One-Tap Exploratory Data Analysis
docs.text:
import pyscio as sc

df = sc.read("clinical_trial.csv")
eda_report = df.scio.eda()
print(eda_report.summary())
eda_report.to_html("eda_report.html")

docs.title: 2. Autonomous Hypothesis Testing & Formula Interface
docs.text:
# Standard group comparison (checks normality, CLT, pathology, and variance homogeneity)
res = df.scio.compare(x="treatment_arm", y="recovery_days")
print(res.summary())

# Wilkinson formula syntax (single predictor or multivariate ANCOVA/OLS)
res_formula = df.scio.compare("recovery_days ~ treatment_arm + baseline_score")

docs.title: 3. Multivariate Regression (OLS HC3 & IRLS Logistic)
docs.text:
# Ordinary Least Squares with MacKinnon-White HC3 heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors
ols_res = sc.ols(df, "recovery_days ~ age * C(treatment_arm)", robust_se="HC3")
print(ols_res.summary())

# Binary Logistic Regression with Odds Ratios and McFadden's Pseudo-R²
log_res = sc.logistic(df, "remission ~ age + C(treatment_arm)")
print(log_res.to_df())

docs.title: 4. Stateless Functional Kernels (pyscio.functional as F)
docs.text:
import pyscio.functional as F

# Welch's t-test returning a 6-field TTestResult NamedTuple
t_res = F.welch_t(group_a, group_b)
print(t_res.stat, t_res.p, t_res.dof, t_res.ci)

# Exact Non-Central t Confidence Intervals for Hedges' g and Cohen's d
g = F.hedges_g(group_a, group_b)
g_ci = F.hedges_g_ci(group_a, group_b, conf_level=0.95)

# BCa Bootstrap CI & Yuen-Welch Robust Trimmed t-Test
ci_bca = F.bootstrap_ci(group_a, n_resamples=5000, method="bca", seed=42)
yuen_res = F.yuen_t(group_a, group_b, trim=0.2)

docs.title: 1. Distributional Pathology Guards & Large-\(N\) CLT
docs.text:
For large sample sizes (\(N \ge 500\)), formal normality tests (Shapiro-Wilk, D'Agostino-Pearson \(K^2\)) reject normality for negligible deviations. However, naive moment-based Central Limit Theorem (CLT) overrides (\(|\gamma_1| < 1.0 \land |\gamma_2| < 2.0\)) can be fooled by symmetric heavy-tailed, zero-inflated, or bimodal distributions.

pyscio enforces a 3-stage pathology screen (F.check_pathology) before permitting a CLT override:

  1. Point-Mass / Zero-Inflation Guard: Rejects parametric routing if the maximum single-value tie proportion \(\max_v \frac{\#\{x_i = v\}}{n} \ge 0.30\).
  2. Heavy-Tailed / Cauchy Scale Guard: Compares sample standard deviation against the Gaussian-calibrated interquartile scale: $\(R_{\text{tail}} = \frac{s}{\text{IQR} / 1.34898}\)$ If \(R_{\text{tail}} > 2.2\) or the fraction of observations outside Tukey's outer fences \([Q_1 - 3\text{IQR}, Q_3 + 3\text{IQR}]\) exceeds \(2.5\%\), parametric routing is blocked.
  3. Sarle's Bimodality Coefficient (\(BC\)): $\(BC = \frac{\gamma_1^2 + 1}{\gamma_2 + 3 \frac{(n-1)^2}{(n-2)(n-3)}}\)$ If \(BC > 0.555\) alongside platykurtic excess kurtosis (\(\gamma_2 < -0.5\)), the distribution is flagged as bimodal/multimodal and routed to non-parametric inference.

docs.title: 2. Exact Non-Central \(t\) Confidence Intervals for Effect Sizes
docs.text:
Rather than relying on symmetric normal approximations for Cohen's \(d\) and Hedges' \(g\), pyscio inverts the cumulative distribution function of the Non-Central \(t\)-distribution (\(F_{t, u}(\cdot; \lambda)\)) via Brent's root-finding method (scipy.optimize.brentq):

\[F_{t, u}(t_{ ext{obs}}; \lambda_L) = 1 - rac{\alpha}{2}, \qquad F_{t, u}(t_{ ext{obs}}; \lambda_U) = rac{\alpha}{2}\]

where \(\lambda = d \sqrt{ rac{n_1 n_2}{n_1 + n_2}}\) for independent two-sample designs.

docs.title: 3. MacKinnon-White HC3 Robust Covariance
docs.text:
In sc.ols, default standard errors use the finite-sample bias-corrected HC3 jackknife sandwich estimator:

\[\hat{\Sigma}_{\text{HC3}} = (X^T X)^{-1} X^T \operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{e_i^2}{(1 - h_{ii})^2}\right) X (X^T X)^{-1}\]

where \(h_{ii} = x_i^T (X^T X)^{-1} x_i\) is the \(i\)-th diagonal element of the projection (hat) matrix.
